djc0cl.q: Vehicle S, reversing to enter the traffic flow, must give way to vehicles coming from both the right and the left
djc0cl.why: A vehicle entering the traffic flow, even by reversing out of a parking space, must give way to traffic from both directions.

ezbaqb.q: Vehicle S, reversing to enter the traffic flow, must use its direction indicators
ezbaqb.why: You must signal the manoeuvre with the direction indicators (indicatori di direzione) before entering traffic, also when reversing out of a parking space.

1lnomsv.q: Vehicle S, reversing to enter the traffic flow, must watch for any pedestrians passing behind it and give them way
1lnomsv.why: When reversing out, you must check for pedestrians behind the vehicle and give them priority.

1i2wzts.q: Vehicle S, reversing to enter the traffic flow, must give way to all vehicles in transit
1i2wzts.why: A driver entering traffic from a parking space must give way to all passing vehicles, from any direction.

1di0s7k.q: Vehicle S, reversing to enter the traffic flow, must make sure the road is clear and perform the manoeuvre with particular caution
1di0s7k.why: Reversing into traffic requires checking that the road is clear and manoeuvring with extra care.

1anrb6a.q: Vehicle S, reversing to enter the traffic flow, must switch on the hazard warning lights
1anrb6a.why: Hazard lights (luci di emergenza) are for breakdowns or danger; for entering traffic the direction indicators are enough.

oa95j8.q: Vehicle S, reversing to enter the traffic flow, must switch on the rear fog light
oa95j8.why: The rear fog light is used only in fog, snow or heavy rain, not for a reversing manoeuvre.

1hbiw97.q: Vehicle S, reversing to enter the traffic flow, must give way only to vehicles travelling in its own direction
1hbiw97.why: The driver must give way to all vehicles, from both right and left, not only those travelling in the same direction.

edk2u1.q: Vehicle S, reversing to enter the traffic flow, must manoeuvre quickly to free up the parking space
edk2u1.why: The manoeuvre must be done slowly and carefully, with no rush to free the parking space.

1uhl2c2.q: Vehicle S, reversing to enter the traffic flow, must sound the horn repeatedly during the manoeuvre
1uhl2c2.why: The horn is used only to warn of immediate danger; it is not to be sounded repeatedly while reversing.

32g9h5.q: It is forbidden, because it creates danger or obstruction to traffic, to keep to the left edge of the carriageway in order to turn into a street on the right
32g9h5.why: To turn right you must stay as close as possible to the right edge; positioning on the left creates danger and obstruction.

14so02y.q: It is forbidden, because it creates danger or obstruction to traffic, to stop on tram tracks
14so02y.why: Stopping on tram tracks (binari tramviari) is prohibited because it blocks trams and creates danger.

tlezeo.q: It is forbidden, because it creates danger or obstruction to traffic, to change direction without signalling the manoeuvre in sufficient advance
tlezeo.why: A change of direction must be signalled well in advance; failing to do so endangers other road users.

1sxbvhl.q: It is forbidden, because it creates danger or obstruction to traffic, to race at speed
1sxbvhl.why: Speed races on public roads are forbidden because they endanger other road users.

v8xzt.q: It is forbidden, because it creates danger or obstruction to traffic, to drive at too low a speed without justified reason
v8xzt.why: Driving too slowly without good reason obstructs traffic and is forbidden.

1jh9l14.q: It is forbidden, because it creates danger or obstruction to traffic, to enter the traffic flow coming from side streets
1jh9l14.why: Joining traffic from side streets is allowed as long as right of way is respected; it is forbidden only when it creates danger.

6t0gp3.q: It is forbidden, because it creates danger or obstruction to traffic, to adjust speed according to the characteristics and conditions of the road
6t0gp3.why: Adapting speed to the road's characteristics and conditions is a duty, not a prohibition.

1buzxha.q: It is forbidden, because it creates danger or obstruction to traffic, to briefly stop a vehicle along the right edge of a one-way carriageway
1buzxha.why: A brief stop along the right edge, even on a one-way road, is allowed if it causes no obstruction.

127a544.q: A driver of a vehicle, even a high-performance one, must in any case not exceed the speed limits set by law
127a544.why: Speed limits apply to all vehicles, regardless of their performance.

1ujl5on.q: A driver of a vehicle, even a high-performance one, must as a rule give way at crossroads to all vehicles coming from the right
1ujl5on.why: At crossroads without signs, the right-hand priority rule applies, even to very powerful vehicles.

1b2e2xh.q: A driver of a vehicle, even a high-performance one, must avoid creating danger for other road users
1b2e2xh.why: Every driver must avoid creating danger or obstruction for others, whatever the vehicle.

19euhwd.q: A driver of a vehicle, even a high-performance one, must look in the rear-view mirror before signalling the intention to change lane
19euhwd.why: Before signalling and changing lane you must check the rear-view mirror to confirm the manoeuvre is safe.

1b2jgd6.q: A driver of a vehicle, even a high-performance one, must keep as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway when making a right turn
1b2jgd6.why: For a right turn you move as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.

1okl22n.q: A driver must always drive in the middle of the road, but without crossing the lane line
1okl22n.why: You must drive on the right side of the carriageway (carreggiata), as close as possible to its right edge, not in the middle.

iauoes.q: A driver must keep the high beams on during the day, even in town
iauoes.why: High beams must not be used in daytime or in town, because they dazzle other road users.

1uzfcke.q: A driver may overtake in any traffic condition, as long as there is no prohibition sign
1uzfcke.why: Overtaking is allowed only if visibility, space and traffic make it safe, even without a prohibition sign.

y152mz.q: A driver must use the horn in built-up areas every time they approach a cycle crossing
y152mz.why: In built-up areas (centri abitati) the horn is forbidden except for immediate danger; it is not used at cycle crossings.

w51guv.q: A driver may fit bitonal horns to be heard more easily, using them only outside built-up areas
w51guv.why: Bitonal horns are not allowed on ordinary vehicles; the horn must be of an approved type with a continuous, uniform sound.

6le0l6.q: Animals may be carried on motorcycles if kept in a proper cage
6le0l6.why: Animals may be carried on motorcycles only inside a proper cage or container.

1tpt0pu.q: Cargo must be placed on motorcycles so that it does not project more than 50 cm to the sides
1tpt0pu.why: On motorcycles, cargo must not stick out more than 50 cm sideways.

p4uyl4.q: Cargo must be placed on motor vehicles so as not to reduce the driver's visibility
p4uyl4.why: Cargo must not reduce the driver's visibility, for safety reasons.

4b4qs2.q: Cargo must be placed on motor vehicles so as not to impede freedom of movement while driving
4b4qs2.why: Cargo must not restrict the driver's freedom of movement while driving.

fgcdvf.q: Cargo must be placed on motor vehicles so as to prevent it from falling
fgcdvf.why: Cargo must be arranged and secured so that it cannot fall onto the road.

zhjkd3.q: Cargo must be placed on motor vehicles so that it does not project from the rear by more than three tenths of the vehicle's length
zhjkd3.why: Cargo may project from the rear by at most three tenths of the vehicle's length.

188sr1s.q: Cargo on motor vehicles must not exceed the load capacity stated in the registration document (carta di circolazione)
188sr1s.why: The load must not exceed the capacity stated in the registration document (carta di circolazione).

2l17l7.q: Cargo must be placed on motor vehicles so as to avoid its lateral projection by more than three tenths of the vehicle's length
2l17l7.why: Cargo must not stick out sideways beyond the vehicle's outline; the three-tenths limit applies to the rear projection.

yye0xw.q: Cargo must be placed on motor vehicles so as not to exceed the maximum height stated in the registration document by more than 10%, but within 4 metres
yye0xw.why: Cargo cannot exceed the maximum permitted height of 4 metres; there is no 10% tolerance on height.

56i5vx.q: Cargo must be placed on motor vehicles so as not to exceed the useful load stated in the registration document by more than 10%
56i5vx.why: The load capacity in the registration document cannot be exceeded, not even by 10%.

1wjijxe.q: Cargo must be placed on motor vehicles so as to project from the front of the vehicle by more than three tenths of its length
1wjijxe.why: Cargo cannot project at the front beyond the permitted limit; front overhang is very restricted.

e17t9k.q: Cargo must be signalled by day with a red cloth if it projects from the rear
e17t9k.why: Rear projecting cargo is marked with the special square panel with white and red stripes, not with a red cloth.

yjxsdx.q: The rear projection of cargo must be marked with a retroreflective panel with yellow and red stripes
yjxsdx.why: The retroreflective panel for projecting cargo has white and red stripes, not yellow and red.

1cu9wax.q: On motorcycles it is in no case permitted to carry a load
1cu9wax.why: Carrying a load on motorcycles is allowed, within the size limits and if securely fastened.

2medon.q: On motorcycles it is permitted to carry shopping bags even if not firmly secured
2medon.why: Loads on motorcycles must be firmly secured; unsecured shopping bags are dangerous and not allowed.

1urqe3g.q: Correct use of the road means that vehicles proceed at a speed suited to road and traffic conditions
1urqe3g.why: Speed must be adapted to road and traffic conditions.

13p8mo6.q: Correct use of the road means that behaviour rules and common prudence are observed
13p8mo6.why: You must follow the behaviour rules and use common prudence.

1kdsqqj.q: Correct use of the road means hurrying to clear the junction when a steady yellow light appears and you cannot stop safely before the stop line
1kdsqqj.why: On a steady yellow, if you cannot stop safely before the stop line, you clear the junction.

mme384.q: Correct use of the road means giving way to pedestrians crossing at pedestrian crossings
mme384.why: Pedestrians on pedestrian crossings (attraversamenti pedonali) have priority.

y0aaxv.q: Correct use of the road means using dipped headlights in built-up areas at night
y0aaxv.why: At night in built-up areas you use dipped headlights (anabbaglianti).

z79pln.q: Correct use of the road means checking the rear-view mirrors before operating the indicator to change lane
z79pln.why: Before signalling a lane change you check the rear-view mirrors.

qe066t.q: Correct use of the road means that vehicles always enter the carriageway as quickly as possible
qe066t.why: Entering the carriageway must be done carefully and with right of way respected, not as fast as possible.

151ohaj.q: Correct use of the road means always stopping at pedestrian crossings and moving off only if no pedestrians approach
151ohaj.why: You stop only if pedestrians are crossing or about to cross, not every time.

xyabv3.q: Correct use of the road means using high beams in every case
xyabv3.why: High beams are used only outside built-up areas on unlit roads, and never to dazzle others.

1zcwir.q: Correct use of the road means stopping in every case when facing the sign shown
1zcwir.why: The sign is Give way (Dare precedenza): you stop only when needed to let vehicles with priority pass.

1r97p13.q: Correct use of the road means proceeding at high speed so as not to cause obstruction
1r97p13.why: Speed must suit the conditions, not be high; speeding creates danger.

189x797.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must follow the direction allowed by any road markings
189x797.why: If you chose the wrong pre-selection lane (corsia di preselezione), follow the direction allowed by the road markings.

8qre6w.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must not change lanes, also so as not to obstruct following vehicles
8qre6w.why: Do not change lanes: it would be dangerous and obstruct the vehicles behind.

1kyl48a.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must not brake suddenly, to avoid rear-end collisions and confusion in traffic
1kyl48a.why: Braking suddenly can cause rear-end collisions and confusion in traffic.

9jxfjf.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must not stop to ask for information, so as not to hinder the traffic flow
9jxfjf.why: Stopping to ask for directions hinders traffic and creates danger.

17e65xd.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must proceed in the direction indicated by the signs, giving way as required
17e65xd.why: You proceed in the direction required by the signs, respecting right of way.

1ovkbtg.q: Arriving at a junction, if we cannot immediately tell who has right of way, we must proceed with prudence and care
1ovkbtg.why: When unsure about priority, proceed cautiously, slowing down if needed.

k9b7vy.q: Arriving at a junction, if we cannot immediately tell who has right of way, we may continue without slowing down if we choose to go straight
k9b7vy.why: When priority is unclear you must slow down and proceed carefully, even when going straight.

19mds48.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must make the turn we intended, giving way to all vehicles
19mds48.why: You cannot turn in a direction other than the one allowed by your lane and the markings.

p367op.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must ask traffic officers for advice
p367op.why: You do not stop to ask for advice: you follow the direction allowed by the signs and markings.

1ifckay.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must switch on all direction indicators simultaneously as a danger signal
1ifckay.why: Hazard lights are not for this mistake; you continue in the permitted direction.

n3wo61.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must pull over to the right and stop until the column of following vehicles has passed
n3wo61.why: Pulling over and stopping is dangerous and obstructs traffic; follow the permitted direction.

fedo8n.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we try to reverse carefully to the point where the continuous lane lines end
fedo8n.why: Reversing on the carriageway to fix a mistake is forbidden and very dangerous.

nfbggg.q: When, approaching a junction, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must reach the traffic light and wait for the light to allow us to change lane
nfbggg.why: You do not wait for the light to change lanes; you follow the direction allowed by the markings.

imgxlo.q: In a built-up area, when a pedestrian outside the crossing stripes does not seem to give us way, we must reduce speed and, if necessary, stop so as not to hit them
imgxlo.why: The driver must slow down and stop if necessary, to avoid hitting the pedestrian.

6a5ygf.q: In a built-up area, when a pedestrian outside the crossing stripes does not seem to give us way, it is advisable to slow down and warn them with a short horn blast in case of immediate danger
6a5ygf.why: In case of immediate danger, a short horn blast is allowed even in built-up areas, after slowing down.

ompx4v.q: In a built-up area, when a pedestrian outside the crossing stripes does not seem to give us way, we must reduce speed until stopping in time, if necessary
ompx4v.why: You must reduce speed until you can stop in time, if necessary.

tbmojv.q: In a built-up area, when a pedestrian outside the crossing stripes does not seem to give us way, at night it is advisable to proceed with high beams on so that they notice us
tbmojv.why: High beams in built-up areas are forbidden and would dazzle the pedestrian; you must slow down.

1b1f4ax.q: In a built-up area, when a pedestrian outside the crossing stripes does not seem to give us way, it is advisable to try to attract their attention by any means so that they give us way
1b1f4ax.why: You cannot use any means you like: the horn is allowed only for immediate danger, and you must slow down anyway.

1p89ryf.q: In a built-up area, when a pedestrian outside the crossing stripes does not seem to give us way, we must continue without paying attention to them because we have right of way
1p89ryf.why: Even with priority, the driver must avoid hitting the pedestrian and use caution.

gmb7x0.q: When, in a built-up area, a vehicle driver encounters a procession, they must stop on the right and wait for the carriageway to clear
gmb7x0.why: Facing a procession (corteo), you must stop on the right and wait for the road to clear.

qk03s0.q: When, in a built-up area, a vehicle driver encounters a procession, they must avoid sounding the horn
qk03s0.why: With a procession you avoid the horn, which is forbidden in built-up areas without immediate danger.

1mapa84.q: It is advisable for a driver who encounters a procession in a built-up area to turn into a side street if possible, provided the manoeuvre can be done correctly
1mapa84.why: If possible and without improper manoeuvres, turning into a side street avoids obstructing the procession.

5vc9ak.q: When a driver in a built-up area comes across a procession, they must make sure it has completely passed before going through.
5vc9ak.why: A procession must not be broken up. You may proceed only once the whole procession (corteo) has passed.

1qaxgyj.q: A driver who comes across a procession in a built-up area should avoid reversing if this obstructs the flow of traffic.
1qaxgyj.why: Reversing in the way of other traffic creates an obstruction and a hazard. The driver should wait for the procession to pass.

lunxnx.q: A driver who comes across a procession in a built-up area should not make a U-turn if this obstructs traffic.
lunxnx.why: A U-turn that obstructs traffic must be avoided. The driver waits until the procession has passed.

tunemc.q: When a driver in a built-up area comes across a procession, they must sound the horn discreetly to warn the procession to clear the way as soon as possible.
tunemc.why: You must not use the horn to hurry a procession. In built-up areas the horn is only for immediate danger, so you wait for it to pass.

za6ptv.q: When a driver in a built-up area comes across a procession, they must try to make their way through it, interrupting it, but with extreme caution.
za6ptv.why: A procession (corteo) may not be cut through, even carefully. The driver must wait until it has completely passed.

ho5t7i.q: A driver who comes across a procession in a built-up area should switch on the main beam headlights to see better and avoid accidents.
ho5t7i.why: Main beams (luci di profondità) are not allowed in lit built-up areas and would dazzle people. With a procession you simply wait.

1iw4u50.q: A driver who comes across a procession in a built-up area, if in a great hurry, should pass quickly while sounding the horn continuously.
1iw4u50.why: You may not overtake or break up a procession, and the horn is not for hurrying people. You must wait for it to pass.

n3hd9s.q: When a driver in a built-up area comes across a procession, they must act according to its density, passing it or breaking through it if possible.
n3hd9s.why: The density of the procession makes no difference. It may never be passed or broken up; you wait for it to pass completely.

ifpdza.q: When a driver in a built-up area comes across a procession, they must quickly reverse to the nearest junction.
ifpdza.why: Reversing quickly is a dangerous manoeuvre and is not required. The driver stays put and waits for the procession to pass.

vvpo24.q: At an urban junction, when the vehicle ahead is slow to move off at the green signal, it is appropriate to wait patiently for it to start moving.
vvpo24.why: When the light turns green and the car ahead is slow, you should be patient and wait for it to move off.

xg68px.q: At an urban junction, when the vehicle ahead is slow to move off at the green signal, it is appropriate to avoid insistent horn use and not to provoke impatience in other drivers.
xg68px.why: Insistent honking is pointless and not allowed to hurry someone, and it stirs up impatience in other drivers.

lgz2ti.q: At an urban junction, when the vehicle ahead is slow to move off at the green signal, it is appropriate, if needed and if it can be done safely, to help the driver who has stopped.
lgz2ti.why: If needed and safe, helping a driver who has stalled or stopped is the right civic behaviour.

1iau1fd.q: In built-up areas it is forbidden to use the horn to urge the driver ahead to move off when the traffic light turns green.
1iau1fd.why: In built-up areas the horn (segnalatore acustico) may only be used to avoid immediate danger, not to hurry the driver ahead.

eycm02.q: At an urban junction, when the vehicle ahead is slow to move off at the green signal, you must not overtake it with dangerous manoeuvres.
eycm02.why: Another driver's delay does not justify a dangerous manoeuvre. Overtake only if allowed and safe.

13d7qrl.q: At an urban junction, when the vehicle ahead is slow to move off at the green signal, it is appropriate to sound the horn insistently to urge the driver to start moving.
13d7qrl.why: Insistent honking is improper and, in towns, not allowed to hurry someone. Wait patiently instead.

1qvbr8c.q: At an urban junction, when the vehicle ahead is slow to move off at the green signal, it is appropriate to use the horn to draw the attention of the drivers behind.
1qvbr8c.why: In towns the horn is only for immediate danger. Here there is none, so honking only causes confusion and tension.

1tme2bp.q: At an urban junction, when the vehicle ahead is slow to move off at the green signal, it is appropriate to pull the handbrake and get out to look for a traffic officer to take action.
1tme2bp.why: Leaving your vehicle in the middle of a junction is dangerous and obstructive. Just wait patiently.

1cqghzg.q: At an urban junction, when the vehicle ahead is slow to move off at the green signal, it is appropriate to clear the carriageway as soon as possible, even by reversing direction.
1cqghzg.why: Making a U-turn at a junction is dangerous and often prohibited. Wait for the vehicle ahead to move off.

1q8li80.q: When meeting a vehicle with its main beams on, at night on a non-urban road, you must proceed carefully using dipped headlights.
1q8li80.why: If dazzled, proceed with caution using dipped headlights (anabbaglianti), and do not answer with main beams.

83xn85.q: When meeting a vehicle with its main beams on, at night on a non-urban road, you must look away from the beam of light so as not to be dazzled.
83xn85.why: Looking away from the beam, towards the right edge of the road, reduces dazzle.

1pakbfr.q: When meeting a vehicle with its main beams on, at night on a non-urban road, you must slow down adequately and, if necessary, stop.
1pakbfr.why: Dazzle reduces visibility, so you must slow down and, if you cannot see, stop safely.

1bm45yr.q: When meeting a vehicle with its main beams on, at night on a non-urban road, you must take the reduced visibility into account in how you drive.
1bm45yr.why: Dazzle reduces visibility, so your driving must adapt with lower speed and more attention.

p408o4.q: When meeting a vehicle with its main beams on, at night on a non-urban road, you must avoid sudden manoeuvres and lane changes.
p408o4.why: With reduced visibility, sudden moves or lane changes are dangerous. Keep a steady course.

mzzfgq.q: When meeting a vehicle with its main beams on, at night on a non-urban road, you must set the interior rear-view mirror to the anti-dazzle position.
mzzfgq.why: The dazzle comes from the oncoming vehicle in front of you. The anti-dazzle mirror setting only helps against headlights from behind.

pm5l8r.q: When meeting a vehicle with its main beams on, at night on a non-urban road, you must in turn drive with main beams to see the road better.
pm5l8r.why: Answering with main beams dazzles the other driver and adds danger. Use dipped headlights.

5ckr1c.q: When meeting a vehicle with its main beams on, at night on a non-urban road, you must stop immediately.
5ckr1c.why: There is no need to stop at once. Slow down and stop only if you cannot see enough.

1gm4f09.q: When meeting a vehicle with its main beams on, at night on a non-urban road, you must sound the dual-tone horns to attract the attention of the oncoming vehicle.
1gm4f09.why: The right signal is a brief flash of the headlights (lampeggio), not the horn, which is not appropriate here.

z5sskm.q: When meeting a vehicle with its main beams on, at night on a non-urban road, you must try to shield your eyes with your hands.
z5sskm.why: Covering your eyes with your hands means losing control. Keep both hands on the wheel and look away from the beam.

1fwwiki.q: In order not to be a danger or obstruction to traffic, you must drive in a way suited to the characteristics of the vehicle, the road and the traffic.
1fwwiki.why: Driving must suit the vehicle, the road and the traffic. That is how you avoid causing danger or obstruction.

bz1eih.q: In order not to be a danger or obstruction to traffic, you must observe not only the traffic rules but also the precautions dictated by common sense.
bz1eih.why: Besides the rules, a driver must use caution and common sense, since rules cannot cover every situation.

14jbpfv.q: In order not to be a danger or obstruction to traffic, you must combine application of the basic traffic rules with a strong sense of civic duty.
14jbpfv.why: Following the rules should go together with civic sense and respect for other road users.

d8onfj.q: In order not to be a danger or obstruction to traffic, you must merely observe the maximum speed limits.
d8onfj.why: Obeying the limits is not enough. Speed must also suit traffic, visibility, the road and the vehicle.

bj2ivs.q: In order not to be a danger or obstruction to traffic, you must always drive at a constant speed.
bj2ivs.why: Speed must adapt to conditions, so it changes. You cannot always keep it constant.

10i6yt1.q: In order not to be a danger or obstruction to traffic, you must in any case give way to all vehicles at junctions.
10i6yt1.why: Right of way follows signs and rules, not everyone. Whoever has priority should go ahead.

ihu299.q: In order not to be a danger or obstruction to traffic, you must merely observe the minimum speed limits.
ihu299.why: Observing minimum limits alone is not enough. You must adapt speed to conditions and traffic and follow all the rules.

jd21u.q: In heavy traffic the driver must adjust their speed, matching as closely as possible the speed of the flow of traffic in the lane being used.
jd21u.why: Matching the speed of the traffic flow avoids sudden braking and obstruction and keeps traffic moving.

1pvq6za.q: In heavy traffic the driver must always keep the safety distance from the vehicle ahead.
1pvq6za.why: The safety distance (distanza di sicurezza) must always be kept, especially in heavy traffic, so you can brake without hitting the car ahead.

h32d9s.q: In heavy traffic the driver must avoid sounding the horn to urge the vehicles ahead to speed up.
h32d9s.why: The horn warns of danger. It is not for urging vehicles ahead, which cannot speed up in traffic anyway.

102reei.q: In heavy traffic the driver must repeatedly change lanes so as to always occupy the freest one.
102reei.why: Constant lane changing is dangerous and obstructive. Stay in your lane and follow the flow.

149nc9y.q: In heavy traffic the driver must occupy the lanes reserved for public service vehicles if they are free.
149nc9y.why: Reserved lanes are off limits to other vehicles even when empty and even in heavy traffic.

t0g93v.q: In heavy traffic the driver must use the simultaneous flashing of all the direction indicators.
t0g93v.why: Hazard lights are used only in specific cases such as emergencies or danger, not simply for heavy traffic.

8ixt9i.q: To turn right you must keep as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.
8ixt9i.why: For a right turn you stay as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.

1qkpnwy.q: To turn right you must signal the manoeuvre in advance by using the direction indicator.
1qkpnwy.why: Every turn must be signalled early with the indicator (indicatore di direzione) to warn other road users.

t4lkvf.q: A right turn is made by moving into the lane that allows that manoeuvre.
t4lkvf.why: You move in good time into the lane that allows the turn, so you do not obstruct traffic going straight.

10bgj7q.q: A right turn is made by reducing speed as you get closer to the turning point.
10bgj7q.why: You slow down gradually as you approach the turn, so you can make it safely.

1kurx0i.q: A right turn is made without creating danger or obstruction to others.
1kurx0i.why: Every manoeuvre, including a turn, must be made without endangering or obstructing anyone.

7txlsh.q: To turn right you must keep as close as possible to the left edge of the carriageway.
7txlsh.why: For a right turn you keep near the right edge, not the left.

j6d5wv.q: To turn right you must stay in the left lane.
j6d5wv.why: For a right turn you take the right-hand lane, not the left.

z08ay.q: A right turn is made without ever giving way to pedestrians if the traffic light is showing green.
z08ay.why: Even on green, a turning driver must give way to pedestrians crossing on the zebra crossing.

v79iwv.q: A right turn is made by going around the illuminated column that may be placed in the centre of the junction.
v79iwv.why: A right turn hugs the right edge. You do not go around the centre of the junction.

3v8lqw.q: When you want to turn right you must move close to the centre of the junction.
3v8lqw.why: For a right turn you stay near the right edge. Moving toward the centre applies to left turns.

1wgxxmd.q: On a three-lane two-way road, as shown, the middle lane must be used only for overtaking.
1wgxxmd.why: On a three-lane two-way road, the middle lane (B) is used only for overtaking, by traffic from either direction.

1onedln.q: On a two-lane two-way road, as shown, the left lane must be used only for overtaking.
1onedln.why: Traffic keeps to the right-hand side. The left lane is used only to overtake.

v0ai9.q: On main extra-urban roads, stopping is allowed only in the designated areas.
v0ai9.why: On main extra-urban roads (strade extraurbane principali) parking is allowed only in the designated parking areas.

nx0fn8.q: On a road with two separate carriageways, as shown, you must use the right carriageway for normal driving and the left one for overtaking.
nx0fn8.why: Each separate carriageway carries traffic in one direction only. Overtaking is done in the lanes of your own carriageway.

1fcnzjr.q: On roads made up of one carriageway with two lanes and two-way traffic, as shown, you may drive in parallel lines.
1fcnzjr.why: On a two-lane two-way road each direction has only one lane, so you cannot drive in parallel lines.

uxuf69.q: On roads with four separate carriageways, the central ones are reserved for overtaking.
uxuf69.why: Each carriageway carries traffic in one direction only, so none is reserved for overtaking.

o2vdbl.q: Anyone intending to change lane must check that the lane they want to enter is clear ahead for a sufficient distance.
o2vdbl.why: Before changing lanes you must check there is enough clear space ahead in the target lane.

mn0i8d.q: Anyone intending to change lane must check that the lane they want to enter is clear behind for a sufficient distance.
mn0i8d.why: You must check your mirrors to be sure no vehicles are approaching from behind in the target lane.

10xwfvq.q: Anyone intending to change lane in order to overtake must check that the vehicle ahead has not signalled the start of the same manoeuvre.
10xwfvq.why: Before overtaking, make sure the vehicle ahead has not signalled that it is about to overtake too.

11x1fu1.q: Anyone intending to change lane must signal the manoeuvre in advance using the direction indicator.
11x1fu1.why: Every lane change must be signalled early with the indicator (indicatore di direzione).

19uibd7.q: Anyone intending to change lane must not cause obstruction or danger to those using the lane they want to enter.
19uibd7.why: A lane change must not endanger or obstruct those already in the destination lane.

8es57b.q: Anyone intending to change lane must not use the direction indicator if the road is clear.
8es57b.why: You must always signal a lane change, even on an empty road, because other users may be out of sight.

qivci0.q: Anyone intending to change lane is obliged to signal the manoeuvre by using the audible warning device (horn).
qivci0.why: The manoeuvre is signalled with the indicator. The horn is not required and is only for danger.

1x73d.q: Before changing lane you must check that the lanes are separated by a continuous line.
1x73d.why: Before changing lane you must check the line is broken. A continuous line cannot be crossed.

mwwyfo.q: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must move towards the centre of the carriageway.
mwwyfo.why: For a left turn you move close to the centre line of the road, so you do not block traffic going straight.

irefcx.q: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must normally occupy the left area of the junction, like the vehicles shown, unless otherwise indicated.
irefcx.why: At a junction a left turn normally passes to the left of the centre point, as the vehicles N and A show.

c7nhjb.q: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must go around the centre of the junction like vehicle H shown, if there is a roundabout sign.
c7nhjb.why: With the roundabout sign (rotatoria) you go around the centre of the junction, like vehicle H, keeping it on your left.

1a83up6.q: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must give way to vehicles coming from the right, unless otherwise indicated.
1a83up6.why: Without signs, a driver turning left must give way to vehicles coming from the right.

1hyaz3w.q: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must move as far as possible to the left edge of the carriageway.
1hyaz3w.why: For a left turn you move toward the centre of the road, not to the left edge.

1jmir5v.q: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must carry out the manoeuvre quickly to avoid vehicles coming from the right and the left.
1jmir5v.why: The turn must be made carefully at moderate speed, giving way as required. Rushing adds danger.

7xkyy0.q: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must always make the turn by occupying the right side of the junction, like the vehicles shown.
7xkyy0.why: A left turn normally goes to the left of the centre of the junction, not always on the right side.

1exoykl.q: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must give way to vehicles arriving from the left, unless otherwise indicated.
1exoykl.why: You give way to vehicles from the right, not from the left, unless signs say otherwise.

10sx4d6.q: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must sound the horn so as to cross the junction more safely.
10sx4d6.why: The horn is not used for turning. It is only for immediate danger. Safety comes from respecting right of way.

1i208gg.q: Vehicles must normally travel on the right-hand part of the carriageway and close to the right edge.
1i208gg.why: The general rule is to drive on the right-hand part of the carriageway, close to the right edge.

bx4382.q: On a road divided into two separate carriageways as shown, vehicles must normally travel on the carriageway to the right of their direction of travel.
bx4382.why: With separate carriageways you use the one on the right of your direction of travel, in the lanes marked A.

1m2d6hw.q: On a road divided into three separate carriageways as shown, vehicles must normally travel on the central carriageway or the one on their right in relation to their direction of travel.
1m2d6hw.why: With several separate carriageways, vehicles normally use the central one or the one on their right relative to their direction of travel.

4c8v3i.q: On a two-way carriageway with two lanes, as shown, vehicles must travel in the right-hand lane, using only the left one for overtaking.
4c8v3i.why: On a two-way road with two lanes you keep to the right; the left lane (corsia di sinistra) is only for overtaking.

1qnyrk2.q: On carriageways with three lanes per direction, as shown, motor vehicles must normally use the freest lane on the right.
1qnyrk2.why: On three-lane carriageways, motor vehicles normally use the free lane furthest to the right.

5ue2js.q: Motor vehicles may travel in parallel lines near junctions controlled by traffic officers or traffic lights.
5ue2js.why: Driving in parallel lines (file parallele) is allowed near junctions controlled by officers or traffic lights, where vehicles queue across lanes.

1tc99w1.q: Anyone leading animals must keep them as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.
1tc99w1.why: Animals being led must be kept as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway to cause the least obstruction.

m5uz84.q: On two-way roads with two lanes, as shown, when passing other vehicles you must move as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.
m5uz84.why: When meeting oncoming vehicles you leave as much side space as possible by moving close to the right edge of the carriageway.

drj2pc.q: On a two-way carriageway with two lanes, as shown, vehicles must travel in the right-hand lane, using the left one only for overtaking.
drj2pc.why: On a two-way road with two lanes you keep right and use the left lane only to overtake.

fv4fi.q: On a two-way road with two lanes, as shown, vehicles going uphill over a crest must keep as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.
fv4fi.why: Going up to a crest your view is limited, so you keep as far right as possible to avoid hitting oncoming traffic.

1smmopf.q: On a two-way road with three lanes, as shown, vehicles may use the central lane for normal driving.
1smmopf.why: On a two-way road with three lanes, the central lane is reserved for overtaking and is not for normal driving.

1uxh0gh.q: When a road is two-way with three lanes, as shown, vehicles may travel in parallel lines.
1uxh0gh.why: Parallel-line driving (file parallele) is not allowed on two-way roads with three lanes; you keep to the right.

1tcwj3j.q: To turn left, vehicles must keep to the right edge of the carriageway.
1tcwj3j.why: To turn left you move towards the centre of the road (or the left edge on one-way streets), not the right edge.

f0h3po.q: It is possible to drive in the middle of the carriageway when the road is empty.
f0h3po.why: You must always keep to the right, even if the road is empty; driving in the middle of the carriageway is not allowed.

jhfuuu.q: On a two-way road with two lanes, as shown, vehicles may travel in parallel lines.
jhfuuu.why: On a two-way road with one lane per direction there are no parallel lines (file parallele); you keep to the right.

3u2tiu.q: In heavy traffic it is permitted to travel in parallel lines, using the lanes reserved for buses and public service vehicles.
3u2tiu.why: Lanes reserved for buses and public service vehicles must never be used for parallel-line driving, even in heavy traffic.

1rd84vs.q: On a one-way road, vehicles going round a left-hand bend must keep close to the left edge of the carriageway.
1rd84vs.why: Even on one-way roads you normally keep right in a bend; the left edge is only used when turning left.

lop6ep.q: On a road with two separate carriageways, as shown, vehicles going over a crest must keep close to the left edge of the carriageway.
lop6ep.why: Over a crest you keep as far right as possible in your direction of travel, even with separate carriageways.

19qpyx8.q: Vehicles going round a bend, on a road with two lanes in each direction, as shown, may drive over the broken line if the road is clear.
19qpyx8.why: In a bend you must stay in your own lane and not cross the lane line, even if it is broken and the road is clear.

ljfgch.q: Vehicles intending to turn left must keep as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.
ljfgch.why: A vehicle turning left moves towards the centre of the road on its own side, not to the right edge.

1fl8mlr.q: Trolleybuses must normally travel as close as possible to the left edge of the carriageway.
1fl8mlr.why: Trolleybuses (filobus) also normally keep to the right of the carriageway, like any other vehicle.

1invhn.q: On roads with 2 lanes per direction, in heavy traffic mopeds may travel in the left lane.
1invhn.why: Mopeds (ciclomotori) must keep right and may not use the left lane, which is for overtaking, even in heavy traffic.

11skbdk.q: On a carriageway as shown, in heavy traffic mopeds and motorcycles may use the cycle lane if they do not exceed 20 km/h.
11skbdk.why: The cycle lane (pista ciclabile) is for bicycles only; mopeds and motorcycles may not use it, whatever their speed.

3ud3v.q: In heavy traffic, motorcycles may use emergency lanes.
3ud3v.why: Emergency lanes (corsie di emergenza) are only for emergencies and rescue vehicles; motorcycles may not use them because of heavy traffic.

5fiq2n.q: On roads with 2 lanes per direction, in heavy traffic two-wheeled mopeds may travel in the left lane.
5fiq2n.why: Mopeds must keep right and may not use the left lane, which is for overtaking, even in heavy traffic.

16gpngf.q: When you want to change lane you must not obstruct or endanger vehicles in the lane you are about to enter.
16gpngf.why: You may change lane only if you do not obstruct or endanger vehicles already in the lane you want to enter.

rc6k6x.q: When you want to change lane you must signal the manoeuvre in advance.
rc6k6x.why: Before changing lane you must signal in good time so other road users can react.

1h50bum.q: When you want to change lane you must check that the lane you want to enter is clear ahead for a sufficient distance.
1h50bum.why: Before changing lane you check there is enough free space ahead in the new lane so nobody has to brake suddenly.

11lmke4.q: When you want to change lane you must check that the line separating the lanes is broken (dashed).
11lmke4.why: You may change lane only where the dividing line is broken; a continuous line may not be crossed.

x5qi7l.q: When you want to change lane you must signal the manoeuvre by using the direction indicator.
x5qi7l.why: A lane change is signalled with the direction indicator (indicatore di direzione), in advance and until the manoeuvre is complete.

7ph6pm.q: When you want to change lane you must check that no other vehicles are approaching in the lane you want to occupy.
7ph6pm.why: Before moving over you check that no vehicles are approaching in the target lane, including from behind.

pyhcu6.q: In urban roads, when you want to turn, it is permitted to drive straddling the lane lines.
pyhcu6.why: You may never drive straddling lane lines, even in town or when turning; you position yourself fully within a lane.

diopvz.q: When you want to change lane, using the direction indicator is optional if there are broken (dashed) lines.
diopvz.why: Signalling with the indicator is always compulsory when changing lane, even where the lines are broken.

1oss1md.q: When you want to change lane, to move into the right-hand lane, no particular care is needed.
1oss1md.why: Moving to the right lane also requires care: you check the lane is clear and signal the manoeuvre.

htemh.q: Near junctions, as shown, you can always change lane up to the transverse stop line.
htemh.why: Close to the junction the lane lines become continuous and changing lane is no longer allowed; you must position yourself earlier.

1k8ymr4.q: When you want to change lane for overtaking, it is compulsory to reduce speed.
1k8ymr4.why: Overtaking does not require slowing down; you actually need to be faster than the vehicle you are passing, within the limits.

1r2fjtx.q: When you want to change direction you must operate the direction indicator in advance.
1r2fjtx.why: Before changing direction you switch on the indicator in good time to warn other road users.

i9cvqz.q: To turn left you must normally leave the centre of the junction on your right, like the vehicles shown.
i9cvqz.why: When turning left you pass to the left of the junction centre, so the centre stays on your right.

1vlwur5.q: On a one-way road, to turn left you must keep to the left edge.
1vlwur5.why: On a one-way road you move to the left edge of the carriageway to turn left.

1g64adr.q: While performing a U-turn the direction indicator must stay on for the whole duration of the manoeuvre.
1g64adr.why: During a U-turn (inversione di marcia) the indicator stays on throughout, to show other road users what you are doing.

1ageat7.q: The vehicle shown can turn right.
1ageat7.why: The vehicle is in a middle lane with continuous lines and another lane on its right; to turn right it must be in the right-hand lane.

qohtdg.q: To turn left you must go around the centre of the junction, like the vehicles shown.
qohtdg.why: Normally you do not go around the junction centre when turning left; you leave it on your right.

c3upns.q: When you want to change direction it is compulsory to use sound signals (horn).
c3upns.why: To change direction you use the indicator; the horn is only used to avoid danger.

1g5z5sm.q: Travelling on a three-lane carriageway, as shown, you must use the central lane to turn left.
1g5z5sm.why: To turn left you must use the left-hand lane, not the central one.

wk4mt2.q: On a two-way road, to turn left you must not enter the road you are turning into on the wrong side.
wk4mt2.why: After turning left you enter the right-hand lane of the new road; you must not drive on the wrong side.

1cp75as.q: On a two-way road, when turning left you must normally leave the centre of the junction on your right, like the vehicles shown.
1cp75as.why: When turning left you pass to the left of the junction centre, leaving it on your right.

1djykht.q: On a two-way road, to turn left you must move into the lanes that allow you to continue in that direction.
1djykht.why: To turn left you move early into the lanes that allow you to go in that direction.

fetpo9.q: On a two-way road, to turn left you must move to the left of the continuous centre line.
fetpo9.why: You may not cross a continuous centre line (mezzeria); to turn left you move towards the centre but stay on your side of it.

1ha36my.q: On a two-way road, to turn left you must stay along the right edge of the carriageway.
1ha36my.why: To turn left you move towards the centre of the carriageway, not along the right edge.

swus59.q: On a two-way road, to turn left you must stop before completing the manoeuvre, even if no vehicles are approaching.
swus59.why: You stop only when needed to give way; if nothing is approaching you complete the turn without stopping.

tdzha5.q: On a one-way carriageway, a left turn is made by signalling the manoeuvre in advance.
tdzha5.why: Even on a one-way road you signal a left turn in advance with the indicator.

izzkes.q: During parallel-line driving it is permitted to change lane to make turning manoeuvres.
izzkes.why: Even during parallel-line driving you may change lane to turn, taking the proper precautions.

1kqpdqs.q: Parallel-line driving is permitted when authorised by traffic officers.
1kqpdqs.why: Driving in parallel lines (file parallele) is allowed when traffic officers authorise it.

1z442o.q: Parallel-line driving is permitted on roads with two lanes per direction at a junction controlled by traffic lights.
1z442o.why: Parallel-line driving is allowed near junctions controlled by traffic lights on roads with several lanes per direction.

1e22xu3.q: On roads with at least two lanes per direction, as shown, if traffic is heavy you may travel in parallel lines.
1e22xu3.why: On roads with at least two lanes per direction, parallel-line driving is allowed when traffic is heavy.

f111bk.q: As a rule, it is permitted to travel in parallel lines along the stretch of road leading to a junction controlled by traffic officers.
f111bk.why: On the approach to a junction controlled by traffic officers you may drive in parallel lines to ease the flow.

1jwii5a.q: In heavy traffic on a one-way carriageway with three lanes, as shown, it is permitted to travel in parallel lines.
1jwii5a.why: On a one-way carriageway with several lanes and heavy traffic, parallel-line driving is allowed.

527boy.q: On a one-way carriageway, a left turn is made by entering any lane, if travelling in parallel lines.
527boy.why: Even in parallel-line driving, to turn left you must be in the left-hand lane, not just any lane.

15s9pol.q: It is permitted to travel in parallel lines along the stretch of road leading to a junction not controlled by traffic lights or traffic officers.
15s9pol.why: Near junctions without lights or officers parallel-line driving is not allowed; you keep right.

vd22hh.q: It is permitted to travel in parallel lines on a road with two lanes and two-way traffic, like the one shown.
vd22hh.why: With only one lane per direction you cannot drive in parallel lines; you need at least two lanes per direction.

d7ayon.q: It is always permitted to travel in parallel lines if the two-way carriageway has at least two lanes in each direction, like the one shown.
d7ayon.why: Parallel-line driving is allowed only under particular conditions (heavy traffic, controlled junctions), not always.

tu1xrv.q: In built-up areas it is permitted to drive in parallel lines in any traffic conditions.
tu1xrv.why: Even in built-up areas parallel-line driving is allowed only in heavy traffic or particular conditions.

7ij8ng.q: It is compulsory to travel in parallel lines on carriageways with three lanes per direction, like the one shown.
7ij8ng.why: With three lanes per direction, parallel-line driving is not compulsory; it is only a possibility in specific cases.

v0y80z.q: During parallel-line driving, when travelling in the left lane, you must keep the left direction indicator on.
v0y80z.why: In parallel-line driving the indicator is not kept on; it is used only to change lane or direction.

14eddmq.q: Parallel-line driving is not permitted if the road has only one carriageway.
14eddmq.why: Parallel-line driving is also allowed on a single carriageway, if it has at least two lanes per direction.

1nrug3x.q: During parallel-line driving motorcycles may proceed by passing between the side-by-side vehicles.
1nrug3x.why: Even in parallel-line driving motorcycles may not pass between vehicles driving side by side.

1ekd0fi.q: At junctions you must give way to vehicles running on rails (trams and trains), unless otherwise signalled.
1ekd0fi.why: You give way to rail vehicles unless signs say otherwise, since they cannot swerve or stop quickly.

dd6gh4.q: You must give way to the right and to the left when, from a standstill, you enter the traffic flow.
dd6gh4.why: When you start moving from a standstill into traffic you give way to vehicles from both right and left.

ubl5mv.q: You must give way to all vehicles on the road when making a U-turn.
ubl5mv.why: When making a U-turn (inversione di marcia) you give way to all traffic, as it is a hazardous manoeuvre.

suvych.q: You must give way to all vehicles when reversing.
suvych.why: When reversing (retromarcia) you give way to all vehicles and pedestrians.

rzg4by.q: You must give way to the right and to the left when leaving a driveway (passo carrabile).
rzg4by.why: When leaving a driveway (passo carrabile) you give way to traffic from both right and left.

pgl2s2.q: You must give way to the right and to the left when you see the sign shown.
pgl2s2.why: The STOP sign requires you to stop and give way to vehicles coming from both right and left.

1bkhhfj.q: You must give way to the right and to the left when you see the sign shown.
1bkhhfj.why: The crossroads sign with right-of-way to the right requires you to give way only to vehicles from the right.

1nzedut.q: You must give way to the right and to the left when you see the ROTATORIA sign.
1nzedut.why: The ROTATORIA (roundabout) sign means you give way only to traffic already on the ring (from the left), not from the right.

1qjxe7n.q: You must give way to all vehicles at junctions controlled by a flashing yellow traffic light.
1qjxe7n.why: A flashing yellow light signals caution: the normal right-of-way rules apply, not giving way to everyone.

1ooewsq.q: You must give way to all vehicles on the road when turning left.
1ooewsq.why: When turning left you give way to oncoming traffic and, where relevant, vehicles from the right, not to all vehicles.

ditmtw.q: You must give way to all vehicles on the road when you see the sign shown.
ditmtw.why: The sign shows a junction where your road has priority over the side road; you do not give way to everyone.

3m0np3.q: When approaching a junction you must be ready to observe the right-of-way rules.
3m0np3.why: When approaching a junction you must slow down and be ready to follow the right-of-way rules.

51azpy.q: When approaching an intersection, you must move in good time into the lane for the direction you intend to take.
51azpy.why: You must get into the lane for your intended direction early, so you do not obstruct other vehicles.

t0gsg.q: When approaching an intersection, you must signal your intention to turn in good time.
t0gsg.why: The turn signal (indicatore di direzione) must be switched on early so other road users understand your manoeuvre.

dpm5x.q: When approaching an intersection on a two-wheeled vehicle, you must queue behind the other waiting vehicles.
dpm5x.why: Riders of two-wheelers must also join the queue behind waiting vehicles rather than pushing past them.

1nwp64p.q: When reaching an intersection, you may enter it only if you are able to continue through and clear it.
1nwp64p.why: You must not enter an intersection unless you can drive through and clear it, otherwise you block traffic.

tc680e.q: When approaching an intersection, you must use the greatest caution to avoid accidents.
tc680e.why: Intersections are conflict points, so maximum caution is required to avoid accidents.

pzd1rl.q: When approaching an intersection, you must always go before vehicles coming from the right.
pzd1rl.why: Under the general rule you must give way to vehicles coming from the right (precedenza a destra), not go before them.

1n879kj.q: When approaching an intersection, you must quickly overtake on the left if you want to turn right.
1n879kj.why: To turn right you move to the right in good time. Overtaking on the left near an intersection is dangerous and not allowed.

1tzcm2i.q: When approaching an intersection in built-up areas, you must sound the horn.
1tzcm2i.why: In built-up areas the horn may be used only to warn of immediate danger; it is not compulsory at intersections.

t03c07.q: Near or at intersections, it is not allowed to zigzag, even if the lanes are marked by broken (dashed) lines.
t03c07.why: Near intersections you may not weave between lanes, even when the lane lines are dashed.

n9hu82.q: Near or at intersections, it is not allowed to suddenly change direction.
n9hu82.why: Sudden changes of direction at intersections are dangerous; manoeuvres must be prepared and signalled in advance.

1pq9x3r.q: Near or at intersections, it is not allowed to make a U-turn.
1pq9x3r.why: U-turns (inversione di marcia) are prohibited near and at intersections.

u4oner.q: At extra-urban intersections, parking is not allowed.
u4oner.why: Outside built-up areas, parking (sosta) is prohibited at intersections.

aueij.q: At extra-urban intersections, stopping is not allowed.
aueij.why: Outside built-up areas, even a brief stop (fermata) is prohibited at intersections.

1hyovks.q: Near or at intersections, it is not allowed to overtake a bicycle if you must enter the opposite lane.
1hyovks.why: Near intersections overtaking is forbidden if it takes you into the opposite lane, even for a bicycle.

ooxzb.q: Near or at intersections, it is not allowed to use dipped headlights.
ooxzb.why: Dipped headlights are always allowed and often compulsory; there is no such ban at intersections.

msx4n4.q: Near or at extra-urban intersections, it is not allowed to exceed 60 km/h.
msx4n4.why: There is no fixed 60 km/h limit at extra-urban intersections. The road's normal limit applies, and you should slow down for safety.

tmkuqs.q: At urban intersections, you may omit the turn signal when turning right.
tmkuqs.why: The turn signal must always be used when turning, left or right, including in town.

1j9idt2.q: Near or at intersections controlled by traffic lights, overtaking is not allowed.
1j9idt2.why: The ban on overtaking near intersections does not apply to those controlled by traffic lights.

1i8fjg4.q: Near or at intersections, you do not have to slow down if the traffic light shows a flashing yellow.
1i8fjg4.why: A flashing yellow light requires you to slow down and proceed with caution, observing right of way.

1tzehmb.q: Near or at extra-urban intersections, it is not allowed to use audible warning devices (horn or trumpets).
1tzehmb.why: Outside built-up areas the horn may be used to warn of danger or signal your presence when needed.

i0ony0.q: If two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time from different roads, the duty to give way normally falls on the driver of the vehicle arriving from the left.
i0ony0.why: Under the right-hand rule, the driver who has the other vehicle on their right must give way, so the one arriving from the left yields.

1mltu1x.q: If two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time from different roads, both must reduce speed to avoid accidents.
1mltu1x.why: Even the driver with right of way must slow down near an intersection to avoid accidents.

vl0fq4.q: When reaching an intersection, you must be cautious and tolerant towards anyone who goes first even though they do not have right of way.
vl0fq4.why: You must anticipate others' mistakes: even with right of way, stay cautious if someone goes first anyway.

1p839yk.q: When leaving private property in a vehicle, you must proceed with caution.
1p839yk.why: When leaving private property you are entering a public road, so you must proceed with caution.

1o259px.q: When leaving private property in a vehicle, you must give way to any pedestrians.
1o259px.why: A driver leaving private property must give way to pedestrians and other road users.

12u6zlr.q: When leaving private property in a vehicle, you must proceed slowly, especially when reversing.
12u6zlr.why: Leave private property slowly, especially in reverse, because visibility is limited.

1fp8dfk.q: If two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time from different roads, the duty to give way falls on the driver of the vehicle on the narrower road.
1fp8dfk.why: Road width is irrelevant; without signs the right-hand rule decides who gives way.

f4dhl5.q: When leaving private property in a vehicle, it is compulsory to sound the horn.
f4dhl5.why: Sounding the horn is not compulsory; you must instead proceed carefully and give way.

1aci3oq.q: When leaving private property in a vehicle, you have priority over pedestrians.
1aci3oq.why: A driver leaving private property must give way to pedestrians and has no priority over them.

tkyp2h.q: If a road train (autotreno) intends to turn right into a narrow road, other drivers must bear in mind that it may slow down considerably.
tkyp2h.why: A road train has long, difficult manoeuvres, so it may slow down a lot when turning into a narrow road.

gekw4o.q: If a road train (autotreno) intends to turn right into a narrow road, other drivers must bear in mind that during the manoeuvre it may move to the left (swing wide).
gekw4o.why: To turn right, a road train may need to swing out to the left, taking part of the adjacent lane.

1m7s4x9.q: If a road train (autotreno) intends to turn right into a narrow road, you must not stay too close to it, so as not to obstruct it if it needs to reverse.
1m7s4x9.why: Keeping back lets the road train reverse if it cannot complete the turn in one go.

qsoys8.q: If a road train (autotreno) intends to turn right at an intersection, you must give up overtaking it, because it may block your view of signs or of vehicles coming from the side.
qsoys8.why: A heavy vehicle can hide signs and side traffic, so overtaking is dangerous and should be avoided.

9o0xz.q: If a road train (autotreno) intends to turn right into a narrow road, you must overtake it immediately on the left.
9o0xz.why: Overtaking a road train on the left as it turns right is dangerous, because it may swing out to the left.

zz77xv.q: If a road train (autotreno) intends to turn right into a narrow road, the drivers of following vehicles must overtake it as soon as it turns on its indicator.
zz77xv.why: When it signals, the road train must be left to manoeuvre; do not overtake, slow down and wait.

vafgas.q: If a road train (autotreno) intends to turn right into a narrow road, the drivers of following vehicles must switch on the hazard warning lights.
vafgas.why: Hazard lights are only for danger or obstruction; here you simply slow down and keep your distance.

6uahrl.q: A driver who intends to make a U-turn on a two-way road must give way to approaching vehicles.
6uahrl.why: A driver making a U-turn must give way to approaching vehicles.

lxz6v.q: A driver who intends to make a U-turn on a two-way road must give up the manoeuvre if traffic is heavy and continuous.
lxz6v.why: With heavy, continuous traffic a U-turn creates danger or obstruction, so it must not be attempted.

hwgsg6.q: A driver who intends to make a U-turn on a two-way road must give up the manoeuvre if visibility is poor.
hwgsg6.why: U-turns are not allowed in poor visibility, as other users cannot see the manoeuvre.

oh5mcc.q: A driver who intends to make a U-turn on a two-way road must use the turn signal.
oh5mcc.why: Like any change of direction, a U-turn must be signalled with the turn indicator.

v9kwtt.q: A driver who intends to make a U-turn on a two-way road must not create danger or obstruction to other road users.
v9kwtt.why: A U-turn is allowed only if it creates no danger or obstruction for other road users.

1ogv49g.q: A driver who intends to make a U-turn on a two-way road must switch on the hazard warning lights.
1ogv49g.why: For a U-turn you use the turn signal; hazard lights are not required.

1mn0job.q: A driver who intends to make a U-turn on a two-way road may do so even on a bend, as long as they give way to all vehicles.
1mn0job.why: U-turns are forbidden near bends even if you give way, because visibility is limited.

y7o3ou.q: A driver who may make a U-turn on a two-way road must check whether the centre line is continuous.
y7o3ou.why: What matters is that the manoeuvre is safe and causes no obstruction; checking the centre line alone is not the deciding condition.

eyyyh8.q: A driver who intends to make a U-turn on a two-way road may do so even in poor visibility, if the centre line is dashed.
eyyyh8.why: In poor visibility a U-turn is always forbidden, even when the centre line is dashed.

1bkrjh2.q: A driver who intends to make a U-turn on a two-way road may do so only on wide roads that allow it in a single manoeuvre.
1bkrjh2.why: A U-turn may be done in several manoeuvres, as long as it is safe and causes no obstruction.

15386l8.q: On two-way roads, it is not allowed to make a U-turn near or at bends.
15386l8.why: U-turns are prohibited near bends, where visibility is limited and other drivers cannot see the manoeuvre.

9yfq5.q: U-turns are not allowed near or at intersections.
9yfq5.why: Reversing direction is prohibited near and at intersections.

1xpckr9.q: On two-way roads, it is not allowed to make a U-turn in all cases of poor visibility.
1xpckr9.why: U-turns are forbidden whenever visibility is poor, because they endanger everyone.

13s8ijd.q: On two-way roads, it is not allowed to make a U-turn near or at humps (crests).
13s8ijd.why: U-turns are also prohibited near crests (dossi), where visibility is inadequate.

tntgk5.q: When there are no road markings, U-turn manoeuvres are not allowed.
tntgk5.why: Missing road markings do not ban U-turns; they remain allowed if safe and not in prohibited places.

ziwl7t.q: If the edge line of the carriageway is continuous, it is not allowed to make a U-turn.
ziwl7t.why: The edge line only marks the edge of the carriageway and does not prohibit U-turns.

1ax8hxo.q: Outside built-up areas, it is not allowed to make a U-turn.
1ax8hxo.why: Outside built-up areas U-turns are allowed if safe and not in prohibited places such as bends, crests and intersections.

1i6bqzb.q: On motorways with three lanes in each direction, it is allowed to make a U-turn.
1i6bqzb.why: On motorways U-turns are always prohibited, whatever the number of lanes.

semms6.q: When reaching an intersection controlled by a roundabout, you must give way to vehicles coming from the left only if there is a GIVE WAY sign.
semms6.why: The duty to give way to vehicles already in the roundabout (coming from the left) applies only where there is a GIVE WAY (DARE PRECEDENZA) sign.

kefaz5.q: At intersections controlled by a roundabout, in the absence of a specific sign, the general rule of giving way to the right applies.
kefaz5.why: With no specific sign, the general rule of giving way to the right (precedenza a destra) applies.

1fky8oa.q: At intersections controlled by a roundabout, traffic may be regulated so that entering vehicles give way to those already circulating in the ring.
1fky8oa.why: With the proper signs, entering vehicles must give way to those already on the ring.

v1v9zu.q: At an intersection controlled by a roundabout, the duty to give way may be imposed on vehicles about to enter.
v1v9zu.why: The duty to give way can be imposed on entering vehicles by the GIVE WAY sign.

11b3eag.q: When reaching an intersection controlled by a roundabout, before entering it is advisable to reduce speed and use the greatest caution, while watching the behaviour of other users.
11b3eag.why: Before entering a roundabout you should slow down and watch other users to avoid accidents.

16exs10.q: On a steep road, if vehicles cannot easily pass each other, it is generally the driver going downhill who must stop and, if necessary, reverse.
16exs10.why: Generally the downhill driver yields, since it is easier for them to stop and reverse.

utane8.q: With the GIVE WAY sign, if you need to stop, you must do so at the transverse line made up of a series of white triangles.
utane8.why: If you must stop, do so at the transverse line of white triangles (the give way line).

7084oh.q: When reaching an intersection controlled by a roundabout, it is compulsory to give way to vehicles coming from the left.
7084oh.why: Giving way to vehicles in the ring applies only where there is a GIVE WAY sign; otherwise the right-hand rule applies.

1r8rw07.q: To enter an intersection controlled by a roundabout, you must always give way to vehicles already circulating inside the roundabout.
1r8rw07.why: Not always: without a GIVE WAY sign the general right-hand priority rule applies.

xcoblm.q: At an intersection controlled by a roundabout, vehicles circulating in the ring may reverse.
xcoblm.why: Reversing is prohibited on the roundabout ring, where traffic moves in one direction only.

jalenl.q: When an intersection is controlled by a roundabout, vehicles circulating inside the ring may overtake on both the right and the left.
jalenl.why: On the ring you may not overtake freely on either side; you follow your lane and the prescribed direction.

l8bm1u.q: With the GIVE WAY sign, you must use caution and reduce speed, but you must stop only if necessary.
l8bm1u.why: At a GIVE WAY sign you slow down and stop only if needed to yield.

q8ztsx.q: If on a steep road passing between vehicles is difficult, and one of the two drivers is near a passing place (piazzola di scambio), it is up to that driver to pull over and let the other pass.
q8ztsx.why: The driver nearer to a passing place (piazzola di scambio) must pull in and let the other through.

1am5ixe.q: At a STOP sign, you do not need to stop if there is no transverse stop line and no vehicles are seen approaching.
1am5ixe.why: A STOP sign always requires a full stop, even with no stop line and no traffic in sight.

dbhj55.q: If on a steep road passing between vehicles is not easily possible, it is generally the driver going uphill who must stop.
dbhj55.why: Generally it is the downhill driver who must stop, and reverse if needed, not the uphill one.

eao2mz.q: Near a signalled intersection, it is allowed to stop on the pedestrian crossing if the pedestrian light is red.
eao2mz.why: You may never stop on a pedestrian crossing, even if the pedestrian light is red, because it blocks pedestrians.

yb18tt.q: Drivers must comply with the danger warnings or instructions shown in illuminated text on police vehicles.
yb18tt.why: Illuminated messages on police vehicles are signals that drivers must obey.

8n3ix9.q: If a police car with its siren on overtakes you and positions itself in front, and has a display on the roof reading "ACCOSTARE" (pull over), you are obliged to stop.
8n3ix9.why: The message ACCOSTARE orders you to pull over and stop at the side of the road.

7qm10i.q: If a police car with its siren on overtakes you and positions itself in front, and has a display on the roof reading "ALT POLIZIA" (police stop), only you are obliged to stop.
7qm10i.why: The ALT POLIZIA message is directed at the vehicle following the patrol, which alone must stop.

1meh3gr.q: When you see on the roof of a police car a display with the illuminated text "INCIDENTE" (accident), you must reduce speed.
1meh3gr.why: INCIDENTE warns of an accident ahead, so you must slow down.

g13coa.q: When you see on the roof of a police car a display with the illuminated text "INCIDENTE" (accident), it means that area is at high risk of accidents.
g13coa.why: It means an accident has just occurred ahead, not that the area is high-risk.

1kd1wnt.q: If a police car with its siren on overtakes you and positions itself in front, and has a display on the roof reading "ACCOSTARE" (pull over), it means you are obliged to turn.
1kd1wnt.why: ACCOSTARE means pull over and stop at the side of the road, not turn.

1jjdsfr.q: If a police car has a roof display showing the illuminated message "RALLENTARE", the obligation applies only to heavy vehicles.
1jjdsfr.why: The lit message "RALLENTARE" (slow down) on a police car is aimed at every driver, not just heavy vehicles.

x456cg.q: A driver who intends to enter the flow of traffic must make sure the manoeuvre can be carried out without creating danger or obstruction to other road users.
x456cg.why: Entering traffic must never create danger or obstruction for other road users.

75jaff.q: A driver who intends to enter the flow of traffic must take into account the position, distance and direction of other road users.
75jaff.why: Before entering traffic you must judge where other users are, how far away and which way they are going, so nobody has to react suddenly.

fljqqi.q: A driver who intends to enter the flow of traffic must use the direction indicator to signal the intention to make the manoeuvre with sufficient advance.
fljqqi.why: The manoeuvre must be signalled early with the indicator (indicatore di direzione) so other users can adapt.

1eglgqx.q: A driver who intends to enter the flow of traffic must give way to vehicles already travelling on the road.
1eglgqx.why: A driver entering traffic must give way to vehicles already moving on the road.

1ahh5jx.q: A driver who intends to enter the flow of traffic may omit the direction indicator if no other vehicles are approaching.
1ahh5jx.why: The indicator must always be used when entering traffic, even if no vehicles are visible, because one may appear unexpectedly.

bpa1s6.q: A driver who intends to enter the flow of traffic must give way to vehicles in transit only if there is a specific sign.
bpa1s6.why: Entering traffic always means giving way to vehicles in transit; no sign is needed.

w30igs.q: A driver entering the flow of traffic must give way to vehicles in transit, except for bicycles.
w30igs.why: You must give way to all vehicles in transit, bicycles included.

1mehroo.q: A motorcycle rider who starts from the edge of the carriageway and enters the flow of traffic must wear and fasten the helmet.
1mehroo.why: The helmet must be worn and fastened before setting off, not just while riding.

17ebnns.q: A car driver who starts from the edge of the carriageway and enters the flow of traffic must fasten the seat belt unless exempt.
17ebnns.why: The seat belt must be fastened before moving off, unless an exemption applies.

798j6d.q: A motorcycle rider who starts from the edge of the carriageway and enters the flow of traffic must switch on the dipped headlight.
798j6d.why: Motorcycles must ride with the dipped headlight (anabbagliante) on, even by day, so it is switched on at departure.

1riyut0.q: A driver who starts from the edge of the carriageway and enters the flow of traffic must check that the road is clear, also looking in the rear-view mirrors.
1riyut0.why: Before moving off you must check the road is clear, including a look in the rear-view mirrors.

1egp2g2.q: A driver who starts from the edge of the carriageway and enters the flow of traffic may fasten the seat belt after completing the manoeuvre.
1egp2g2.why: The seat belt must be fastened before starting the manoeuvre, not after it.

b96gz2.q: A motorcyclist who starts from the edge of the carriageway and enters the flow of traffic may put on the helmet after completing the manoeuvre.
b96gz2.why: The helmet must be put on and fastened before departing, not afterwards.

my82rp.q: The driver of vehicle S in the figure, reversing out to enter traffic, must make sure the road is clear and carry out the manoeuvre carefully.
my82rp.why: A driver reversing out of a parking bay must check that the road is clear and manoeuvre with care.

n46hej.q: The driver of vehicle E in the figure, reversing out to enter traffic, must use the direction indicators.
n46hej.why: Even when reversing out of the bay, the manoeuvre must be signalled with the indicators.

yb2qwu.q: The driver of vehicle S in the figure, reversing out to enter traffic, must give way to all vehicles coming from both the right and the left.
yb2qwu.why: A driver reversing into traffic must give way to vehicles from both right and left.

w9572d.q: The driver of vehicle S in the figure, reversing out to enter traffic, must watch for any pedestrians passing behind the vehicle.
w9572d.why: Pedestrians may walk behind a reversing vehicle, so the driver must watch for them.

ffjqd1.q: The driver of vehicle S in the figure, reversing out to enter traffic, must switch on the hazard warning lights (four flashing lights simultaneously).
ffjqd1.why: Hazard lights (quattro frecce) are for specific cases such as danger or obstruction; leaving a bay is signalled with the indicator.

1dgol7u.q: The driver of vehicle S in the figure, reversing out to enter traffic, must sound the horn throughout the whole manoeuvre.
1dgol7u.why: The horn is only for warning of immediate danger, not for the whole manoeuvre.

vg7re6.q: The driver of vehicle S in the figure, reversing out to enter traffic, must give way to vehicles travelling in its direction, except bicycles.
vg7re6.why: You must give way to all vehicles in transit, bicycles included.

1ggg7gv.q: A driver who intends to stop at the right edge of the carriageway must carry out the manoeuvre without creating danger or obstruction to other road users.
1ggg7gv.why: Stopping at the right edge must also not create danger or obstruction for others.

1umq1kg.q: A driver who intends to stop at the right edge of the carriageway must take into account the position, distance and direction of other road users.
1umq1kg.why: Before stopping you must consider where other users are, how far away and their direction.

176kt2i.q: A driver who intends to stop at the right edge of the carriageway must avoid creating danger for approaching two-wheeled vehicles.
176kt2i.why: Check for approaching two-wheelers before stopping, since they often pass on the right side.

5owp4v.q: A driver who intends to stop at the right edge of the carriageway must signal the intention to make the manoeuvre with sufficient advance.
5owp4v.why: The stop must be signalled early, using the right indicator.

ivw99b.q: A driver who intends to stop at the right edge of the carriageway must avoid sudden braking, to ensure the safety of other road users.
ivw99b.why: Braking gradually avoids a rear-end collision from the vehicle behind.

15hg459.q: A driver who intends to stop at the right edge of the carriageway must carry out the manoeuvre by repeatedly flashing the lights.
15hg459.why: A stop is signalled with the indicator, not by repeated light flashing.

1d60eld.q: A driver who intends to stop at the right edge of the carriageway must signal with sufficient advance by using the hazard warning lights (four flashing lights simultaneously).
1d60eld.why: A stop is signalled with the right indicator; hazard lights are not used for this.

1te2vbn.q: A driver who intends to stop at the right edge of the carriageway may omit signalling the intention to make the manoeuvre if traffic is light.
1te2vbn.why: The manoeuvre must always be signalled, even in light traffic.

575zqb.q: Failure to comply with the rules for entering the flow of traffic results, among other things, in loss of licence points.
575zqb.why: Breaking the rules on entering traffic brings a fine plus a deduction of licence points.

1thuf6t.q: Failure to comply with the rules for entering the flow of traffic does not result in deduction of licence points, but in a fine.
1thuf6t.why: Besides the fine, licence points are also deducted.

1vh42rz.q: If a driver stops at the right edge of the carriageway without signalling the intention with sufficient advance, 4 points are deducted from the driver's licence.
1vh42rz.why: A 4-point deduction is not applied; the violation carries a fine.

1ue5ze8.q: Rear-view mirrors contribute to the driver's panoramic view.
1ue5ze8.why: Mirrors widen the driver's field of view to the rear and sides.

ts7vnk.q: The central rear-view mirror of a car must be adjusted to give a good rear view.
ts7vnk.why: The interior mirror must be set to give a good view behind.

135cldn.q: The central and side rear-view mirrors of a car must be adjusted after the driver's seat position has been adjusted.
135cldn.why: Adjust the seat first, then the mirrors, because your eye position determines the correct mirror setting.

sgamwa.q: The central rear-view mirror of a car must be adjusted to give a view of the entire rear window.
