sgamwa.why: The interior mirror should frame the whole rear window.

egbef5.q: The central rear-view mirror of a car must be positioned so that it falls within the driver's field of vision.
egbef5.why: The mirror must sit within the driver's field of view, without needing to move the head much.

3oygo3.q: The central rear-view mirror of a car is generally designed to minimise distortion of the distance of following vehicles.
3oygo3.why: The interior mirror is flat, so distances appear with little distortion.

1b5gzq0.q: Rear-view mirrors must be used by the driver to check, before turning, that no vehicles are approaching from behind.
1b5gzq0.why: Before turning, check the mirrors to make sure nothing is approaching from behind.

4kvzxr.q: The central rear-view mirror of a car has an anti-glare position to be used at night.
4kvzxr.why: The interior mirror has an anti-glare setting for night driving.

njkywl.q: The anti-glare position of the central rear-view mirror of a car serves to reduce eye discomfort caused by the headlights of following vehicles.
njkywl.why: The anti-glare setting reduces dazzle from the headlights of following vehicles.

14ml80g.q: Rear-view mirrors must be used to check the road behind the vehicle before starting a reverse parking manoeuvre.
14ml80g.why: Before reverse parking, check the road behind with the mirrors.

1lrfepv.q: Rear-view mirrors must be used to check the road behind the vehicle before starting an overtaking manoeuvre.
1lrfepv.why: Before overtaking, check the mirrors to see that nobody behind is already overtaking.

aj7sbk.q: Checking the rear-view mirrors allows an overtaking manoeuvre to be completed safely.
aj7sbk.why: Mirror checks also help finish an overtake safely, so you can move back in once there is enough space.

18wgcw3.q: The anti-glare position of the central rear-view mirror of a car must not be used at night.
18wgcw3.why: The anti-glare position is designed precisely for night use.

133c10e.q: The anti-glare position of the central rear-view mirror of a car cannot be used when driving on a motorway.
133c10e.why: There is no such ban; the anti-glare position can be used anywhere, motorways included.

ng5yw7.q: Rear-view mirrors must be used to check the road behind the vehicle every time one intends to continue straight ahead at a junction.
ng5yw7.why: Mirror checks are for manoeuvres that change direction or position, not for simply going straight through a junction.

xs2vcp.q: The interior lighting of the rear-view mirror comes on when the vehicle's position lights are switched on.
xs2vcp.why: The rear-view mirror has no internal lighting tied to the position lights.

1oz0zez.q: The size of rear-view mirrors is proportional to the vehicle's engine displacement.
1oz0zez.why: Mirror size depends on the vehicle category, not on engine displacement.

1j6mb7p.q: The central rear-view mirror of a car may be removed if the vehicle has a left side mirror.
1j6mb7p.why: The interior mirror is mandatory and cannot be removed, even with a left side mirror.

mhl0is.q: During a reverse parking manoeuvre, it is not necessary to use the rear-view mirrors if the vehicle is fitted with parking sensors.
mhl0is.why: Parking sensors are only an aid; mirrors and direct observation are still required.

1uiz6r.q: The rear-view mirrors, taken together, allow the driver to see the entire area of road behind and around the vehicle.
1uiz6r.why: Mirrors leave blind spots (angoli ciechi) that must be checked by looking directly.

b62ihn.q: Motorhomes may be without rear-view mirrors if they make them too wide.
b62ihn.why: Motorhomes (autocaravan) must also have rear-view mirrors; they are compulsory.

zffwkx.q: The adjustment of rear-view mirrors should normally be carried out while the vehicle is moving.
zffwkx.why: Mirrors are adjusted with the vehicle stationary, before setting off, to avoid distraction while driving.

1c4bj21.q: The external rear-view mirrors of cars may be replaced with others of a different type, provided they have a larger surface.
1c4bj21.why: Mirrors may be replaced only with approved ones; a larger surface alone is not enough.

14blyuo.q: One may drive a car that is temporarily missing its rear-view mirrors, provided the speed does not exceed 50 km/h and the hazard warning lights are kept on.
14blyuo.why: You may not drive without the compulsory mirrors, not even slowly or with hazard lights on.

351hvc.q: The left side rear-view mirror must be adjusted so that the rear of the vehicle is visible in its right third.
351hvc.why: In the left mirror the car's rear should appear in the right third, leaving the rest for the road.

g4vcqx.q: The left side rear-view mirror must be adjusted so as to observe mainly the portion of road beside the vehicle.
g4vcqx.why: The side mirror mainly shows the road alongside, complementing the interior mirror.

krju5x.q: The left side rear-view mirror distorts the perception of the distance and speed of approaching vehicles.
krju5x.why: Side mirrors are convex or aspheric, making vehicles seem farther away and slower than they are.

ht5syz.q: The left side rear-view mirror must be used before starting a lane change to the left.
ht5syz.why: Check the left mirror before moving to the left lane.

1e1usst.q: The left side rear-view mirror must be used before starting an overtaking manoeuvre.
1e1usst.why: Check the left mirror before overtaking to see who is approaching in the overtaking lane.

vbwh5c.q: The left side rear-view mirror must be used before starting a left turn.
vbwh5c.why: Check the left mirror before a left turn to make sure nobody is overtaking.

dvavrf.q: The left side rear-view mirror has a very wide blind spot.
dvavrf.why: The left mirror leaves a large blind spot (angolo cieco) beside the vehicle.

1jld4dk.q: Checking the left side rear-view mirror must be supplemented by a quick direct sideways glance before starting an overtake.
1jld4dk.why: A direct sideways glance covers the blind spot the mirror does not show.

1jvdfb3.q: Before entering the flow of traffic, one must check the left side rear-view mirror and verify with direct observation that the road is sufficiently clear behind and alongside the vehicle.
1jvdfb3.why: To enter traffic safely, use the left mirror and look directly behind and alongside.

zv03u0.q: The left side rear-view mirror must be adjusted so as to monitor the behaviour of any children seated in the back of the vehicle.
zv03u0.why: The side mirror is for watching the road, not the passengers.

iqkpys.q: The left side rear-view mirror must be folded in when driving on narrow mountain roads.
iqkpys.why: The left mirror must stay open and usable while driving.

1fzhqg7.q: In built-up areas it is not necessary to use the rear-view mirrors.
1fzhqg7.why: Mirrors must be used everywhere, built-up areas included.

pp8w6a.q: If a rear-view mirror is used during a merging manoeuvre, it is best not to also check with a direct glance, so as not to distract attention from driving.
pp8w6a.why: A direct look is needed because the mirror does not show the blind spots.

1nxn3mi.q: The rear-view mirrors of two-wheeled vehicles are fixed and cannot be adjusted because vibrations tend to move them from the original position.
1nxn3mi.why: Two-wheeler mirrors are adjustable and must be set before riding.

udf4e.q: The adjustment of rear-view mirrors should be carried out, on average, about every thousand kilometres.
udf4e.why: Mirrors are adjusted whenever the driver or driving position changes, before setting off, not at a mileage interval.

12mo8cq.q: Cars fitted with rear headrests are not equipped with a central rear-view mirror because it would be unusable.
12mo8cq.why: The interior mirror is mandatory even with rear headrests.

o97ibq.q: The central rear-view mirror may be used as a screen for the satellite navigator.
o97ibq.why: The mirror cannot serve as a navigator screen, since it must stay clear for rear vision.
